Consult Summary:
- Adult with asthma and known peanut allergy developed acute upper-lip swelling and breathing difficulty ~30 minutes after eating prawn soup; suspected anaphylaxis. Ambulance called; advised to take antihistamine while awaiting EMS.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive upper-lip swelling beginning ~30 minutes after prawn soup around 7:00 PM; swelling started at left corner of lip and is increasing.
- Associated symptoms: Difficulty breathing; possible chest tightness; dizziness.
- Pertinent negatives: No explicit denials documented.
- Past medical history: Asthma. Known peanut allergy. Prior severe reaction in childhood requiring an injection and hospital visit per mother; another episode ~1 year ago after late-night Chinese food with swelling and breathing difficulty.
- Medications: 
  - Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Antihistamines used intermittently in the past (agent/dose/route/frequency not documented); none initially on hand during this event until mother arrived.
- Allergies: Peanuts. Suspected shellfish (prawn) based on current reaction.
- Social history/preventive: Not detailed. Patient was initially alone; mother later present.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Physical findings: Not recorded (teleconsult; patient-reported lip swelling).

Impression:
- Suspected anaphylaxis following prawn ingestion, with angioedema of upper lip and respiratory difficulty, in a patient with asthma and known peanut allergy.

Plan:
- Emergency actions:
  - Call 999 for ambulance for suspected anaphylaxis.
  - Remain with accompanying person until EMS arrival.
  - Take available antihistamine while awaiting EMS (agent/dose not specified).
- Follow-up:
  - After hospital discharge, patient to contact clinic; clinician to arrange further allergy management and discuss emergency “injections” for future reactions (type not specified).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full medication reconciliation (including doses/routes/frequencies), drug allergy list beyond peanuts, vitals, physical exam, documentation of rash/hives/wheezing, epinephrine auto-injector possession/training, detailed PMH/PSH, smoking/alcohol status, pregnancy status, weight, and clear avoidance counseling.
- Internal conflicts: None significant; patient initially alone then mother arrived (resolved).
- Transcript quality: Some disfluencies/partial sentences; overall adequate to determine emergency management.
